English.Char_Desc_2000:
Song Cleaner tidies a folder of MP3 songs recorded from the radio. Click Choose folder, then 1. Scan: it reads every song and changes nothing. Its pages then show what it proposes: better names (no more "_01" or station tags, "abba-waterloo" put right, cut-off titles finished), copies of the same recording found by their sound, not their names, with the fullest and best-sounding one kept, and talk or noise to trim from the starts and ends. Every proposal has a tick box and Play buttons, so you can listen before deciding. 3. Apply ticked changes does the rest. Nothing is deleted: removed copies and untouched originals go to folders beside your music, and Undo last Apply puts everything back. Trimming never lowers the sound quality. Doubtful names can be looked up in the free AcoustID music database with a free key. Free software under the GPL; its source code comes with it.
Before you install: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer is not code-signed (a signing certificate is a paid yearly service), so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" box: click More info, then Run anyway. A few antivirus programs wrongly flag new unsigned programs; you can check the download against the SHA-256 fingerprint on its release page. No administrator password is needed.

Permissions.Distribution_Permissions: Song Cleaner is free to use and share. Download sites may list it and offer the unchanged Setup.exe, or link to the download page.
Permissions.EULA: Song Cleaner is free and comes with no warranty. Use it at your own risk. The free parts it is built from keep their own licenses, listed in the licenses folder it installs.
